claims: C1 the authority hierarchy has six tiers, ranked highest to lowest: Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, No Authority
C2 No Authority is the sixth tier, below all others, and covers assistant and tool messages, quoted/untrusted text, and multimodal data in other messages
C3 when instructions at different authority levels conflict, the instruction at the higher level overrides the one at the lower level

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: authority level L1 is higher in the six-tier hierarchy than level L2

concepts.name: root_level
concepts.gloss: the Root tier: fundamental root rules that cannot be overridden by system messages, developers or users

concepts.name: system_level
concepts.gloss: the System tier: rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages but not by developers or users

concepts.name: developer_level
concepts.gloss: the Developer tier: instructions given by developers using the API

concepts.name: user_level
concepts.gloss: the User tier: instructions from end users

concepts.name: guideline_level
concepts.gloss: the Guideline tier: instructions that can be implicitly overridden

concepts.name: no_authority_level
concepts.gloss: the No Authority tier, below all others: assistant and tool messages, quoted/untrusted text, and multimodal data in other messages

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is designated with authority level L
concepts.inference: the ordering of authority levels applies to instructions, so each instruction must carry the level it is designated with

concepts.name: conflicting_instructions
concepts.gloss: instructions I and J conflict with each other
concepts.inference: the override rule is stated for the case of conflict, so a relation marking two instructions as conflicting must exist

ontology.gloss: Guideline is higher than No Authority

asserts.read_back: instruction % overrides instruction % because % is at a higher authority level than % and the two conflict
asserts.body: instruction_level(I, L1), instruction_level(J, L2), authority_levels_hierarchy(L1, L2), conflicting_instructions(I, J)

closure.reason: the clause states when a higher-level instruction overrides a lower-level one; it does not prohibit overriding in other cases, so silence leaves overriding permitted
